absent: Numeric encodings of NMI status values, vectors, handler types and priority flags.
Locking and memory ordering guarantees for shared NMI mask and counters beyond the single barrier shown.
Concrete DMA operations, IOMMU platform hooks, swiotlb internals and GART option semantics.
Layouts of trap frame, perf extended state container and platform resource structures.
Boot order and caller context for selftest, speaker, pmem and ROM probing relative to other init phases.
Contention detection criteria, trace payloads and static call update synchronization.
Overflow handling for unknown NMI tally and behaviour when expected failures are configured.

findings.text: Boot time NMI validation installs a temporary unknown event sink, exercises remote and local processor signalling with success expectation, then removes the sink and emits an aggregate verdict distinguishing full success from unexpected failures.

A generic case runner executes a supplied probe, compares a shared failure indicator against the caller expected outcome, updates success versus unexpected failure tallies and total count, reports a compact per case status, and clears the indicator before the next case.

Remote coverage addresses all online processors except the initiator and is skipped when that set is empty, while local coverage addresses only the initiator. The NMI callback marks the current processor complete when its bit was present and reports handled only in that situation.

An IPI probe installs a prioritized local NMI receiver, orders prior state before issuing the NMI vector to a caller mask, waits with a bounded microsecond scale poll for mask exhaustion, always releases the receiver, and records registration versus timeout outcomes in shared status.

Timeout and registration failure share a single status word compared for equality, and the unknown event tally is maintained separately without influencing the final pass fail verdict shown. The source itself questions release behaviour on timeout, indicating lifecycle uncertainty under expiry.

Three visible unlock helpers are provided: a direct native passthrough and two contention aware traced variants for native and paravirtual paths that conditionally emit a release trace before delegating to the underlying unlock.

A predicate recognizes native unlock implementations by querying the current unlock target. Registration swaps plain native and paravirtual unlock targets for their traced counterparts, unregistration performs the inverse swap, and registration always reports success.

Paravirtual lock operations default to inert wait and kick behaviour with a preemption query that constantly reports not preempted. A static branch controlling paravirtual spin lock handling starts in the disabled state.

Early paravirtual support announces the underlying platform name at boot and exposes non instrumentable shims for safe halt and for control and debug register access that forward to native primitives.
Platform identity defaults to bare hardware wording with input output delay enabled and an optional extra user code segment value supplied only in extended paravirtual builds.

The patch template groups operations into processor, interrupt, halt and memory management families. Processor and interrupt slots largely forward to native primitives with inert lifecycle hooks, halt uses native variants, TLB maintenance maps to local global single and multi variants, page table value construction is identity, and allocation release and mapping lifecycle hooks are inert except for native fixmap handling.

DMA and IOMMU control state is held in read mostly storage with build dependent defaults covering a DAC quirk disable flag, a global DMA operations selector, overflow panic and force flags, plus merge and disable and detection indicators.

Software bounce buffering is enabled when physical memory exceeds the 32 bit DMA limit without an explicit disable, or when host or guest memory encryption attributes are present. Xen aware builds add initial domain and frontend conditions and perform remap initialization with Xen DMA operations, while minimal builds provide inert detection.

Early IOMMU allocation takes a Xen paravirtual shortcut when applicable, otherwise it sequences software buffering detection, aperture hole setup, vendor specific detection for two vendors, and generic buffering initialization.

Boot option parsing treats the option string as comma separated keywords that independently toggle merging, forcing, disabling and panic behaviours, warn on obsolete DAC spellings, handle a quirk disable spelling with early return, enable software buffering on request, select passthrough versus translated defaults, and forward each token to aperture option handling.
Late IOMMU initialization invokes the platform init hook, then either logs active software buffering with details or releases buffering resources depending on the enable flag.
A VIA bridge quirk, unless explicitly disabled, traverses the subordinate bus and constrains every discovered device to 32 bit DMA addressing.
Platform speaker setup registers a simple singleton platform device under the conventional speaker name and converts the allocation result into a numeric error status.

Performance register numbering has distinct 32 and 64 bit maxima. A table maps core general registers plus stack pointer, instruction pointer, flags and segment selectors to offsets within the trap frame, with segment entries marked invalid on 64 bit and eight additional extended registers present only on 64 bit.

Extended vector register indices are resolved through an associated extended state block with zero returned when that block is absent, while general indices undergo a bounds check before offset based retrieval from the trap frame.

Validation rejects empty masks and any bit in unsupported or reserved sets. The 32 bit build treats extended registers as unsupported and always reports a 32 bit sampling ABI, while the 64 bit build treats segment registers as unsupported and selects 32 versus 64 bit ABI from the target task mode.
On 32 bit builds user register sampling borrows the current task trap frame directly and labels it with the 32 bit ABI.

NMI aware user sampling uses the live task frame outside NMI, otherwise it guards against interrupting trap frame construction by reporting no registers when the NMI stack overlaps that construction window. When safe it copies the syscall preserved subset into a per processor buffer, fills unsaved general slots with all ones, preserves frame pointer for unwinding, and derives the ABI from the user frame without consulting switchable processor state.
A boot time query reports whether Plug and Play BIOS is disabled by delegating to an architecture helper.

Persistent memory discovery scans for legacy persistent memory descriptors with an always true matcher. Absence yields silent success, otherwise it allocates and adds a singleton legacy persistent memory platform device and propagates allocation or addition failures with cleanup on the latter path.

Firmware ROM windows are described as busy read only memory resources: system window from F0000 to FFFFF, extension window from E0000 to EFFFF, video window from C0000 to C7FFF, plus six adapter slots where the first is pre seeded at C8000 with open end and the remainder start empty.
